title: Period and Phase-Shifted Graph of y = cos(x - pi/2)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the period of the function y = \cos(x - \pi/2) and describe how its graph is obtained from y = \cos x.

steps.title: Identify the Fundamental Period
steps.explanation: The coefficient of x is 1, so the fundamental period remains 2*pi.
steps.why: Horizontal translations do not alter the period of a periodic function.

steps.title: Determine the Horizontal Shift
steps.explanation: The graph of y = cos(x - pi/2) is the graph of y = cos x shifted horizontally to the right by pi/2 units, which coincides identically with y = sin x.
steps.why: Replacing x with x - pi/2 translates the graph right by pi/2; by the cofunction identity, cos(x - pi/2) = sin x.

steps.title: List Key Points Over [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: Over [0, 2*pi], the curve has x-intercepts at 0, pi, 2*pi, a maximum of 1 at x = pi/2, and a minimum of -1 at x = 3*pi/2.
steps.why: These are the shifted quadrantal landmarks of cosine (or equivalently the standard landmarks of sine).
